questions.prompt: 2. Which of these sub-shells contain 5 orbitals?
questions.answer_guide: The d subshell contains 5 orbitals (holding a maximum of 10 electrons).

questions.prompt: 3. Which statement is correct about the position of phosphorus P, in the periodic table?
questions.answer_guide: Phosphorus (atomic number 15) has electron configuration 2,8,5, placing it in Group 5 (or 15) and Period 3.

questions.prompt: 4. First ionization energy generally decrease
questions.answer_guide: First ionization energy decreases down a group due to increased atomic radius and shielding effect.

questions.prompt: 5. Which statement describes what happens during electrolysis?
questions.answer_guide: Electrolysis is the decomposition of ionic compounds using electricity.

questions.prompt: 6. Brass is an alloy, it is made up of copper and
questions.answer_guide: Brass is an alloy composed primarily of copper and zinc.

questions.prompt:
7. Lumps of calcium carbonate react with dilute hydrochloric acid.
Which change in conditions decreases the rate of a reaction.
options: A. Increasing the concentration of the acid
B. Increasing the volume of the acid
C. Increasing the size of the lumps of calcium carbonate
questions.answer_guide: Increasing the size of lumps decreases the surface area exposed to acid, thereby decreasing the rate of reaction.

questions.prompt: Question five: Mole and stoichiometry (10 marks)
items: A. Define the term Mole.
B. What is the concentration in g/dm³ of 0.5 mol/dm³ ethanoic acid (CH3COOH)? (RAM: C=12, O=16, H=1)
C. What is the concentration in mol/dm³ of a solution containing 4 g/dm³ of sodium hydroxide (NaOH)? (RAM: Na=23, O=16, H=1)

D. 2.0 gram of magnesium dissolves in an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen. What volume of hydrogen can be obtained from the 2.0 gram of magnesium at r.t.p?
Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> MgCl2(aq) + H2(g)
questions.answer_guide:
A. A mole is the amount of substance containing 6.02 × 10²³ elementary entities (Avogadro's number).
B. Molar mass of CH3COOH = 60 g/mol. Conc = 0.5 * 60 = 30 g/dm³.
C. Molar mass of NaOH = 40 g/mol. Conc = 4 / 40 = 0.1 mol/dm³.
D. Moles of Mg = 2.0 / 24 = 0.0833 mol. Moles of H2 = 0.0833 mol. Volume of H2 = 0.0833 * 24 dm³ = 2.0 dm³ (or 2000 cm³).

questions.prompt: Question six: Energy in chemistry (9 marks)
questions.diagram: <svg viewBox='0 0 350 100' xmlns='[http://www.w3.org/2000/svg](http://www.w3.org/2000/svg)' style='background:#fff;'><text x='20' y='45' font-size='16'>H — H</text><text x='20' y='85' font-size='16'>H — H</text><text x='90' y='65' font-size='20'>+</text><text x='115' y='65' font-size='16'>C ≡ O</text><text x='180' y='65' font-size='20'>→</text><text x='210' y='65' font-size='16'>CH3OH</text></svg>
items:
A. The equation shows reactants and products for 2 H2 + CO -> CH3OH.
Bond Energies: H-H = 436 kJ/mol, C≡O = 1072 kJ/mol, C-H = 414 kJ/mol, C-O = 358 kJ/mol, O-H = 463 kJ/mol.
i) Show that the molar enthalpy change ΔH for the reaction is -119 kJ/mol.
ii) Explain why this reaction is exothermic?

B. Differentiate between enthalpy and enthalpy change:
i) Enthalpy
ii) Enthalpy change
questions.answer_guide:
A. i) Bonds broken = 2(436) + 1072 = 872 + 1072 = 1944 kJ/mol. Bonds formed = 3(414) + 358 + 463 = 1242 + 358 + 463 = 2063 kJ/mol. ΔH = 1944 - 2063 = -119 kJ/mol.
ii) It is exothermic because energy released forming new bonds (2063 kJ) is greater than energy absorbed breaking old bonds (1944 kJ).
B. i) Enthalpy (H) is the total heat energy content of a system at constant pressure.
ii) Enthalpy change (ΔH) is the amount of heat energy absorbed or released during a chemical reaction.
